definition.def: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able or allowed to go into it.
examples: The facilities have been adapted to give access to wheelchair users. [+ to]
Scientists have only recently been able to gain access to the area. [+ to]
The Mortimer Hotel offers easy access to central London. [+ to]

definition.def: If you have access to something such as information or equipment, you have the opportunity or right to see it or use it.
examples: ...a Code of Practice that would give patients right of access to their medical records. [+ to]
Consultant-led teams will have access to the latest equipment.

definition.def: If you have access to a person, you have the opportunity or right to see them or meet them.
examples: He was not allowed access to a lawyer. [+ to]
He had direct access to the Prime Minister.

definition.def: If you access something, especially information held on a computer, you succeed in finding or obtaining it.
examples: You've illegally accessed and misused confidential security files. [VERB noun]
